not versioning.
Editing node fields beyond what setNodeValidation already covers.

demands.title: Reduce DGE first-run friction: no-ceremony first run + single-step setup

demands.title: Multi-harness agent orchestration — DGE routes each node to the best-fit harness/model, with evidence-gated fallback and cost-aware selection
demands.outcome: DGE becomes harness-agnostic: for each node it recommends a harness (Claude Code, Copilot, Kimi, opencode, Codex, …) and model based on node traits, logs the rationale, and lets config pin any node to override. Different harnesses build different nodes in parallel against one source of truth. When a PRIMARY harness fails on INFRASTRUCTURE (CLI missing, auth, network, timeout — never on a failed evidence gate), DGE falls back to the next harness in the chain. Model selection is cost-aware, matching cheaper models to cheaper tasks. The evidence gate remains sovereign: no routing or fallback path can reach 'done' without proof.
constraints: Parallel execution is REQUIRED — different harnesses build different nodes at once — creating a hard dependency on the concurrency-safe store (graph.json is a single unlocked file today; concurrent writes corrupt it). See GAP-010.
The evidence gate stays sovereign: no routing / retry / fallback path may reach verified or done without proof on disk.
Fallback triggers on INFRASTRUCTURE failure only (CLI missing / auth / network / timeout) — a failed evidence gate must never trigger a harness swap.
The dynamic router is itself an agent judgment; every routing decision must be logged with rationale and be overridable by pinning the node harness/model in config.
non_goals: An installer or marketplace-wiring script — that is first-run setup (DEM-010) not orchestration
A GUI or dashboard for routing; config-driven plus logged rationale is enough for v1
Cross-agent adversarial verify role where agent B reviews agent A — a separate roadmap item that rides on top of this
demands.problem: DGE runs on a single harness today, so it cannot exploit the comparative strengths of different agents/models (e.g. one for coding, another for planning), has no fallback when a harness is offline, and cannot lower cost by matching cheaper models to cheaper tasks. Its own roadmap names harness-neutral, parallel, cross-agent delivery as the destination; nothing delivers it yet.

demands.title: Concurrency-safe delivery store — the canonical graph survives concurrent writes without corruption
demands.source: user (Rafael) — roadmap #1 unlock; surfaced by GAP-010 during DEM-011 intake
demands.outcome: The canonical delivery store stops being a single unlocked file that concurrent writers corrupt. Two or more agents completing independent ready nodes at the same time persist their results with no lost or corrupted writes, and the logical source of truth (graph.json or its fragment set) stays valid and consistent after concurrent completion. This is the sequential bootstrap that unlocks all parallel multi-harness work (DEM-011); it is itself delivered on a single harness because the capability it provides does not yet exist while it is being built.
constraints: graph.json (or its logical equivalent) must remain THE source of truth — any split/fragment/lock design keeps one coherent logical graph.
Backward compatibility: existing single-writer flows (conductor / CLI authoring) must keep working unchanged.
Concurrency safety must be proven by an automated test that actually races writers — not argued in prose.
non_goals: The routing / fallback / cost engine — that is DEM-011 and rides on top of this
Distributed / multi-machine stores or a server; local concurrent processes on one repo is the v1 scope
Cross-team or cross-project demand sharing (DGE stays one-to-many and team-blind by design)
demands.problem: graph.json is a single unlocked file. Two agents writing it concurrently corrupt it — so execution is deliberately sequential today. This blocks the parallel half of DGE's pitch (DEM-011 REQ-047) and caps team scale. It is the roadmap's single highest-leverage unlock.

The shared skeleton is enforced by a cross-renderer test rather than hoped for.

New emoji glyphs beyond what the Next block needs
Restyling the internals of the Mermaid dependency diagram

Run entirely locally and offline with no external assets or network dependency
Require no CDN and no account

Editing graph state from the viewer
Remote hosting or publishing
Authentication or collaboration

demands.title: User-controlled offline viewer refresh
demands.summary: Replace flickering two-second reloads with calm, user-controlled viewer refresh.

demands.title: Harden the evidence gate against an adversarial builder
demands.summary: Seal, cross-family refutation, and holdout criteria so DGE's proven-not-claimed gate holds against an adversarial builder, not just a well-behaved one.
demands.outcome: The evidence gate survives a builder that edits its own contract, overfits to visible checks, or is verified by its own model family. Three tracks: HMAC-sealed validation contracts (Track 1, ~80% of value, ships and is proven first), cross-family refutation for high-risk nodes, and holdout criteria withheld from the builder. Each track is proven by an adversarial attack that must fail, not a feature that must pass.
constraints: Preserve the DAG model the concurrency-safe store (rev-CAS plus exclusive lock) and the append-only evidence manifest
Do not weaken or bypass the waiver escape hatch (done-waived) or the ambiguous-key adjudication rule
All three mechanisms harden the trust primitive and add no new execution capability
The HMAC signing key never enters git; sealing writes go through the existing rev-CAS mutation path
Every gate is fail-closed: an uncheckable seal a missing cross-family verifier or an absent key blocks verification rather than self-certifying
non_goals: OS-keychain key storage (deferred future hardening; key is a git-ignored chmod-600 file for now)
CI-only or verifier-side holdout storage that is truly unreachable from a fully-adversarial local builder (deferred; committed holdout file is the pragmatic 90%)
Any new execution or orchestration capability beyond hardening the existing evidence gate

gaps.question: How is Copilot CLI install proven when the agent cannot run a live Copilot session in this repo?
gaps.resolution: Split proof: automated static schema validation (claude plugin validate + JSON parse) gates the graph now; live Copilot/Claude install is a documented manual checklist captured via 'dge evidence add' after the manifests are pushed to GitHub.

gaps.question: Should the store be a physical demand-centric reorg or a logical demand-grouped view?
gaps.resolution: Both: build a physical demand-centric reorg AND a dge show observability view.

gaps.question: Where does a node that serves requirements from multiple demands physically live?
gaps.resolution: N/A by new model rule: a node belongs to exactly one demand (all its requirement_ids share one demand_id), so no node has two physical parents. Cross-demand shared work is modeled via depends_on between single-demand nodes.

gaps.question: Is this a demand to build now, or a design discussion to answer in prose?

How should AMBIGUOUS be signaled by the validate step so the conductor can distinguish it from PASS/FAIL — a new evidence result state (e.g. --result pass|fail|ambiguous), a conductor-side judgment, or an exit-code convention? This decides whether execute-graph's binary transient/structural classification must change, and ties to the evidence-add --result pass|fail backlog.
gaps.resolution: Split mechanism. Result-ambiguity -> extend 'dge evidence' with --result pass|fail|ambiguous; the done gate treats 'ambiguous' as unsatisfied so a node cannot close on it (productizes the evidence-add-can-falsely-satisfy backlog). Fix-ambiguity -> conductor-side rule bounded by structure: after a FAIL, pause-and-ask only when the repair would exit the node's declared blast radius OR more than one node-satisfying change exists and the contract does not disambiguate; otherwise retry as today. execute-graph gains a third branch (AMBIGUOUS) beyond its transient/structural binary. Minimal, testable engine change.

gaps.question: Is the single-step-setup target ONE command via npm postinstall (auto-runs install-skills on npm install; fewer commands but fires in CI and is 'magic'), or ONE EXPLICIT command like 'dge setup' (runs install-skills [+ optional init]; greppable, no surprise)?
gaps.resolution: Re-scoped: the target is a bootstrap installer (CLI + skills for chosen harnesses), not a bare npm one-liner. Superseded by GAP-009 which picks the delivery vehicle.

gaps.question: Auto-init default path is cwd-relative, so add-demand in a subdirectory could still create a stray delivery-graph/ there. Is default-path + printed-notice enough, or must auto-init also require a project-root marker (.git/package.json) and refuse otherwise?
gaps.resolution: Require a project-root marker (.git or package.json): auto-init creates the store only at the default path AND when a project root is detected; otherwise it refuses with a clear message. Explicit --graph to a missing file still fails loudly. Enforces 'never create a store in the wrong directory'.

gaps.question: Default title value: literal 'Delivery graph' (deterministic) vs repo/folder basename vs package.json name?
gaps.resolution: Literal 'Delivery graph' default title (deterministic, no filesystem guessing), overridable with --title.

gaps.question: Bootstrap installer delivery vehicle: (A) shell script install-delivery-graph.sh + a .ps1 twin (curl|bash; two files); (B) dge setup subcommand run after npm install (one cross-platform code path, explicit); or (C) npx one-shot 'npx github:rafaelolsr/delivery-graph setup' (single command from scratch, cross-platform, reuses install-skills)?
gaps.resolution: C: npx one-shot bootstrap 'npx github:rafaelolsr/delivery-graph setup' — single cross-platform command, reuses install-skills, no .sh/.ps1 twin, no curl|bash.

gaps.question: Parallel multi-harness execution (REQ-047) requires a concurrency-safe store, but graph.json is a single unlocked file today. Is the concurrency-safe store a SEPARATE demand that DEM-011 depends on, or a track inside DEM-011? DEM-011 cannot be 'done' until it exists.
gaps.resolution: Resolved: the concurrency-safe store is its own demand DEM-012 (created), NOT a track inside DEM-011. DEM-011's parallel requirement (REQ-047) depends on DEM-012 being done first. The dependency is wired at plan time: DEM-011's parallel-execution nodes will carry depends_on pointing at DEM-012's store nodes (depends_on is a node-level field). Build order is strict and sequential: DEM-012 first (bootstrapped on a single harness), then DEM-011. This mirrors the ROADMAP split of 'the unlock' vs 'the destination.'

gaps.question: REQ-045 requires distinguishing INFRASTRUCTURE failure (→ fallback) from work/evidence failure (→ block). How is that classification made reliably per harness, so a real code defect can never be laundered into a pass by retrying on another harness?
gaps.resolution: Resolved during intake grilling: fallback is triggered by INFRASTRUCTURE failure ONLY (CLI missing / auth failure / network error / timeout). A failed evidence gate NEVER triggers a harness swap — the node is blocked, full stop. Classification is the adapter's responsibility: each harness adapter must report whether a failure was infra (dispatch could not run) vs work (dispatch ran, evidence failed). This keeps the gate sovereign and closes the 'launder a failing node through harness roulette' hole. Adapter contract detail (how each harness signals the two classes) is captured as GAP-013's adapter-contract scope for the planning pass.

gaps.question: The dynamic router is itself an unproven agent judgment. Beyond 'log the rationale + allow config pin' (REQ-044), what evidence, if any, proves a routing decision was ACCEPTABLE? Or is inspectability + overridability sufficient, with no correctness claim on the pick itself?
gaps.resolution: Resolved: router acceptability = inspectability + overridability with NO correctness claim on the pick itself. Encoded in NODE-042: routeNode always emits source (pin|recommended) + rationale (the inspectable record REQ-044 requires) and honors config pins that override unconditionally. The recommender is a legible deterministic trait rule set (not an opaque model) precisely because the judgment is unproven; a human reads the why and can pin a different choice. No evidence proves a pick correct; the gate still validates the resulting work independently.

gaps.question: Which harnesses are in scope for v1 (Claude Code, Copilot, Kimi, opencode, Codex — all, or a subset)? What is the minimum adapter contract each must satisfy (invoke a task, return a result, report infra availability)?
gaps.resolution: v1 harness matrix = claude + copilot (both already HARNESS_TARGETS in skill-installer; two adapters is the minimum that proves harness-agnosticism). kimi / codex / opencode deferred to fast-follow as adapter-only additions (no engine change). Minimum adapter contract = three ops: id (stable string); available() returning {ok reason} as a cheap infra probe; dispatch(task) returning {class exitCode stdout stderr artifacts} where class is infra_failure / work_failure / ok. The class field mirrors bin/dge.mjs runCapturedEvidence's existing split (spawnSync error = could-not-run = infra; ran-nonzero = work) and drives REQ-045 fallback: fall back iff infra_failure never on work_failure. Full note in NODE-040 evidence.
